expectations.text: Report identifies get()'s docstring/behavior contradiction (says returns None, actually raises KeyError) and ranks it at or near the top
expectations.evidence: Item 1 under 'High severity — docstrings that actively mislead': "The code never returns `None`... raises `KeyError` explicitly on line 30 when the session has expired."

expectations.text: Report flags the nonexistent 'timeout' parameter in put()'s docstring as a false-documentation issue
expectations.evidence: Item 2 (High severity): "The docstring lists a `timeout` parameter... there is no `timeout` parameter... This looks like a stale copy/paste."

expectations.text: Report flags iter_expired() as a generator wrongly documented with Returns:/'a list' instead of Yields:
expectations.evidence: Item 3: "says it 'Returns: A list of session ids that have expired,' but the function is a generator... The docstring should use `Yields:`."

expectations.text: Report flags 'Arguments:' as the wrong section name (should be Args:)
expectations.evidence: Item 2 secondary bullet: "Uses the non-standard section header `Arguments:` instead of `Args:`... not recognized by Google-style docstring tooling."

expectations.text: Report flags the ''' quotes on the class docstring
expectations.evidence: Item 9: "The class docstring uses `'''single quotes'''` while every other docstring in the file uses `\"\"\"`. PEP 257 and the Google style guide prescribe `\"\"\"`."

expectations.text: Report flags the imperative mood / missing period on delete()'s summary line
expectations.evidence: Item 11 flags both: "Missing terminal period" and "Uses imperative mood ('Delete...') while the rest of the file uses descriptive third person... Google style prefers the descriptive form."

expectations.text: Report flags the commented-out code in put() and recommends deletion
expectations.evidence: Item 4: "Dead code should be deleted, not commented out — version control already preserves history... the fossilized code should go."

expectations.text: Report flags the malformed TODO above purge()
expectations.evidence: Item 5: "# TODO fix this later... No owner, issue link, or bug reference (conventional format: `TODO(username):`...)" and notes it is unactionable.

expectations.text: Report flags purge() as missing a required docstring
expectations.evidence: Item 6: "A public method with a non-obvious return value (the count of purged sessions) has no docstring at all."

expectations.text: Findings are ordered by severity: wrong/contradictory documentation before missing contracts before formatting noise
expectations.evidence: Wrong-documentation items (1-3) correctly lead, but within Medium the noise items — commented-out code (item 4) and the malformed TODO (item 5) — are ranked ABOVE the missing-contract items: purge()'s missing docstring (item 6) and undocumented __init__/ttl/lookup_count (item 7). Missing contracts do not clearly precede noise as the assertion requires.

expectations.text: Report gives line references and does not modify the source file
expectations.evidence: Line references throughout (e.g. 'lines 16–31', 'line 59', 'lines 60–65') plus a summary table with locations; report states 'No code was changed', git status for session_store.py is clean, and all planted defects remain present.

summary.notes: Thorough audit that catches every planted defect with line references and leaves the source untouched, but its severity ordering places commented-out code and the malformed TODO above the missing-docstring contract gaps, violating the required wrong-before-missing-before-noise order.
